entries.title: The organization blocks the connection
entries.text: Ask an administrator to follow the selected client's enterprise guide and check server allowlists, connector permissions, and publication requirements. Personal setup does not bypass organization policy.

entries.title: The key type or PKCE configuration does not match
entries.text: Use a key type supported by your client and follow its PKCE instructions. A public client must not depend on a secret. Do not change key type merely to work around an unexplained authentication error.

entries.title: The Connect a Client tab in this guide is disabled
entries.text: Return to Configure a Server and check the Canvas domain, region, and Client ID. Generic MCP also requires at least one callback URI. A recorded client blocker can disable connection even when those fields are complete; see the client issues below.

entries.title: HTTP 400 with DomainRoutingException or a region error
entries.text:
**Why:** The configured MCP endpoint may not match the Canvas account's region, tenant, or production/beta environment. An HTTP 400 without routing details can have other causes.
**Try:** Compare the client's complete MCP Server URL with the endpoint generated by this guide, including /mcp. Use **Which domain and region should I use?** in FAQs to check the domain and region. Do not guess a different region or switch environments to bypass the error.
**Escalate:** If the endpoint is correct and the routing error persists, report it through your institution's Instructure support channel with the client/version, sanitized error, time, endpoint, and expected region and environment.

entries.title: Cannot sign in
entries.text: Ensure your Canvas credentials are correct and that your account has the necessary permissions. If the issue persists, contact your administrator for assistance.

entries.title: 401 Unauthorized when connecting or calling a tool
entries.text:
**Why:** The request may be missing valid authentication, or credentials may have expired, been revoked, or become inactive. A 401 alone does not identify the cause. If the token exchange reports invalid_client, use that separate entry under Clients.
**Try:** Run the selected client's documented sign-in step again and retry a permitted tool call. Check Known Issues for a recorded client blocker. Do not paste tokens into this guide or manually add authorization headers as a workaround.
**Escalate:** Ask your administrator to check the key's active state and the selected client's configuration if fresh sign-in does not resolve the error. Include the client/version, failure stage, sanitized error, HTTP status, and time; never send the token.

entries.title: 403 Forbidden when calling a tool
entries.text:
**Why:** Access may be denied by the user's Canvas permissions, a required scope, or an institution policy. A successful sign-in does not grant access to every Canvas action.
**Try:** Confirm the action appears in **Available Tools** and that you can perform it in Canvas with the same account. Follow the selected client's instructions for requesting https://sso.canvaslms.com/all-client-scopes. Do not grant yourself additional permissions or change a managed developer key.
**Escalate:** Ask your administrator to check the approved key scopes, account permissions, and applicable policies. If those are correct and the failure persists, they can escalate to Instructure with the tool/action, sanitized error, client/version, and time, without including private Canvas data.

entries.title: Prompting Canvas doesn't work as expected
entries.text:
Ensure that your client is correctly configured, and that you are authenticated to Canvas. The MCP only facilitates the connection to Canvas, it does not grant additional permissions or access beyond what your Canvas account allows.
Check that the activity you are attempting to perform is in the **Available Tools** list above and that you have permission in Canvas to perform those actions. If the issue persists, contact your administrator for assistance.

entries.title: The client cannot reach the server
entries.text:
**Why:** Network or organization policies, an incorrect endpoint, or a failed sign-in handshake can prevent a connection. An unreachable endpoint alone does not establish an OAuth defect.
**Try:** Check that the Canvas domain, region, and production or beta environment match the developer key and that the MCP Server URL includes /mcp. Verify your organization's network and client policies.
For Claude web or desktop reporting that it couldn't reach the MCP server, also check the Client ID in the documented advanced connector settings. If the guide calls for reconnecting, use the client's supported workflow to remove and re-add only that connector, preserving other connections. Ask your administrator before changing an organization-managed connector.
**Escalate:** Report persistent failures to your administrator with the client/version, endpoint, failure stage, sanitized error, and time. Check Known Issues before repeating setup.

entries.title: Cannot fetch authorization server metadata
entries.text:
`[AgentHost] Failed to create MCP auth provider for https://<your-domain>.instructure.com/. Failed to fetch authorization server metadata from all attempted URLs.`
**Why:** This is an OAuth discovery failure before Canvas sign-in. The advertised Canvas authorization server's OAuth metadata endpoint returned 404; The MCP's OAuth metadata endpoint returned 200, and Canvas's OpenID metadata endpoint returned 200 but advertised openid. The client did not attempt OpenID fallback.
**Try:** Confirm the MCP URL matches your Canvas domain, environment, and region. Do not add a client secret to a public key, change the callback, or replace the MCP URL with a metadata URL as a workaround.
**Escalate:** Report persistent failures through your Canvas administrator to Instructure, including the client version, error text, time, and attempted metadata URLs or HTTP errors if available. Do not include secrets, tokens, authorization codes, state values, or full authorization URLs.

entries.title: OAuth provider returned `invalid_target`
entries.text:
`invalid_target: The+requested+resource+is+invalid,+missing,+unknown,+or+malformed`
**Why:** The provider rejected the target resource for the OAuth request. Possible causes include a malformed resource URI or a resource that is not approved by the developer key's audience configuration.
**Try:** Check that your configured MCP server URL exactly matches the guide for your Canvas domain, production or beta environment, and region, including /mcp, then retry the guide's sign-in command. The resource identifies the MCP service, not the OAuth callback URI, scope, or your Client ID. Use the documented HTTPS endpoint without a fragment. Do not remove or spoof the resource parameter, change scopes, or disable audience validation as a workaround.
If authorization succeeds but token exchange fails, report that distinction. A client developer or administrator should check the resources requested at both stages and whether the key or audience configuration changed between requests; a valid-looking URL alone does not prove the resource is approved.
**Escalate:** Report to your admin if the error persists or the configuration is managed; ask them to compare the requested resource with the developer key's Allowed Audiences and confirm the correct tenant, environment, region, and active key. Report to Instructure through your admin's support channel if those values are confirmed correct and sign-in still fails. Include the client/version, failure stage, error text, time, configured MCP URL, and sanitized resource value if available. Check Known Issues for a recorded client-specific blocker rather than assuming this error has the same cause in every client.

entries.title: OAuth provider returned `invalid_scope`
entries.text:
`invalid_scope: A+requested+scope+is+invalid,+unknown,+malformed,+or+exceeds+the+scope+granted+by+the+resource+owner.+The+following+scopes+were+requested,+but+not+granted`
**Why:** The OAuth provider rejected a requested scope. The client may have requested a discovered or default scope instead of the Canvas scope, or the developer key may not permit the requested scope.
**Try:** Follow this client's setup instructions and request `https://sso.canvaslms.com/all-client-scopes` exactly. Save the configured scope before login and use the guide's explicit login command rather than relying on automatic scope discovery. If the error occurs during token exchange after successful authorization, include that distinction and have your administrator check the requested scope and resource together.
**Escalate:** Report to Instructure through your admin's support channel if the admin confirms the requested scope and key configuration are correct and the rejection persists. Include the client/version, failure stage, error text, time, and requested scope. An unexpected server_error should also be escalated with its time and sanitized diagnostic rather than worked around by weakening scope or audience checks.

entries.title: invalid_request: Public clients must use PKCE
entries.text:
**Why:** A public key's authorization request must include a PKCE code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256. A missing challenge or an incorrect client configuration can prevent authorization.
**Try:** Use the selected client's documented public-key configuration and PKCE settings, then start a fresh sign-in. Do not add a client secret to a public key. If you are implementing a client, derive the S256 challenge from that sign-in attempt's verifier and send the original code_verifier at token exchange; do not reuse a verifier from a different attempt.
**Escalate:** If the supported client still omits PKCE, report the client/version, key type, failure stage, sanitized diagnostic, and time to your administrator or client maintainer. Do not share the verifier, authorization code, or full sign-in URL.

entries.title: invalid_client or invalid client (401) during OAuth
entries.text:
**Why:** Client authentication failed. A public client without the required PKCE flow or a private client missing its required secret can produce this error; the error alone does not establish which setting is wrong.
**Try:** Confirm the Client ID and key type with your administrator. Public clients must use the documented S256 PKCE flow, including the verifier at token exchange, without a client secret. Private clients must authenticate with their secret even when using PKCE; enter it only in the approved client's secret configuration. Follow the selected guide and start a new sign-in after correcting configuration.
**Escalate:** Ask your administrator to verify the active key and client configuration if the error persists. Include the client/version, public or private key type, authorization or token-exchange stage, sanitized error, and time. Never include the secret or token request credentials.

entries.title: invalid_grant during token exchange
entries.text:
**Why:** The authorization grant may be expired, already used, revoked, or associated with a different client or callback. For PKCE, the verifier may be missing, from a different sign-in attempt, or not match the challenge. Using plain rather than the documented S256 challenge method can also prevent a successful exchange.
**Try:** Start a fresh sign-in using the selected client's guide rather than retrying an old authorization code. Client developers should use code_challenge_method=S256 and send the exact verifier for that attempt on the code's first redemption. Confirm the same approved callback and Client ID are used throughout the flow. Do not log or share authorization codes or verifiers.
**Escalate:** If a fresh attempt still fails, provide the client/version, key type, sanitized diagnostic, failure stage, and time to your administrator or client maintainer. They can verify callback and PKCE handling without collecting the secret values.

entries.title: Copilot Studio connects but tool calls fail
entries.text:
**Why:** Completing the connection does not prove tool invocation works. The current Copilot Studio setup guide includes a temporary Accept-header workaround that may be relevant, but permissions or another request failure can also cause tool calls to fail.
**Try:** Have the connector administrator review the temporary Accept-header policy in the Copilot Studio guide and confirm it was saved with **Update Connector**. Apply only the documented policy if it is applicable to your connector, then retry a safe, permitted tool call. Do not replace authentication settings or grant broader permissions to make the request succeed.
**Escalate:** If the documented setup still fails, report the client/connector version, failing tool, HTTP status, sanitized diagnostic, time, and whether the policy is applied through your administrator's support channel. The workaround should be rechecked against current Copilot releases.

entries.title: redirect_uri does not match client settings
entries.text:
`{"error":"invalid_request","error_description":"redirect_uri does not match client settings"}`
**Why:** The callback URI sent during sign-in does not match the Canvas developer key configuration.
**Try:** Confirm you selected the correct client and install flow and used its documented callback settings. Do not substitute the MCP server URL for the callback.
**Escalate:** Report to your admin to compare the actual `redirect_uri` with the developer key's Redirect URIs, including scheme, hostname, port, path, and trailing slash, and register the exact approved callback. Computed or client-generated callbacks must be confirmed in the client. If you manage the key yourself, make that correction there. Report to Instructure through your admin's support channel if an exact approved match still fails after retrying sign-in. Include the client/version, error text, time, and a sanitized callback URI.

entries.title: MCP server canvas-mcp already exists in local config
entries.text:
**Why:** Your client already has a local server entry named canvas-mcp; adding the same name again would duplicate or overwrite configuration. This is a local configuration conflict.
**Try:** Inspect and update the existing entry using the guide's manual configuration, or use the client's documented remove-and-add workflow, then sign in again. Preserve other servers and settings; do not delete the whole configuration file.
**Escalate:** Report to your admin if the entry is organization-managed or you do not have permission to change it. This message alone does not need to be reported to Instructure.
